clue.text: Possible reason for extra head on everyone

blocks.note: nob is slang for the head
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why everyone was given an extra helping of beer froth, or an extra hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the head piece first in a down light. In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery, and the batting side is awarded an extra run for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra in cricket is a run not scored off the bat, and an illegal delivery is one of the causes of it.

clue.text: Tailored Croatian item of clothing

indicators.note: tailored cloth is cut and stitched into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment made to measure in Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat for wet weather is a kind of garment worn outdoors.

clue.text: Initially up that tree, pals etc playing

indicators.note: playing about, the letters of the companions-and-so-on phrase are put in a new order

blocks.note: someone up a fir tree is in the fir
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Children and their friends start off climbing a tree for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letters signal but is the definition; 'that tree' points to a fir.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the single adverb and the phrase mean at the start or to begin with, as in a list of reasons.

clue.text: Nervous crone in tragedy, gutless

indicators.note: the old woman is placed inside what remains of the sad drama
without its guts a word keeps only its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: outside letters of tragedy
a crone is an ugly old woman, often a witch in stories

explanation.surface: An anxious old hag appears in a weak, spineless tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jumpy and on edge is described as twitchy, a synonym of nervous.

clue.text: Fashion presenter in rambling hypocrite!

indicators.note: the presenter is set inside the word for rambling

blocks.note: a look is a fashion or style
a TV presenter is a host
rambling is walking in the country

explanation.surface: A fashion show presenter is caught out as a hypocrite while going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' looks like an anagram signal but is the hiking word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is the retort aimed at someone who criticises others for a fault they have themselves.

clue.text: Cook particular course, speciality

blocks.note: to do food is to cook it
the main course of a meal

explanation.surface: A chef prepares a special course that is their speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's domain is their field of expertise, their special area.

clue.text: Capital of Latvia seemingly obvious originally, looking north

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each word gives only its first letter
in a down light, facing north means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: Riga, Latvia's capital, appears plain enough when viewed from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Latvia' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Capital' and the initials start at 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Norway, a Scandinavian nation.

clue.text: Isle, a state

blocks.note: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight
taken as written

explanation.surface: An island described as a state of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Today was successful, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: to have won is to have been successful

explanation.surface: Someone remembers that today went well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words refer to the present time, as in 'young people today'.

clue.text: Player of bassoon, or instrument similarly thin, first of all

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface nearly defines the answer too: the oboe is a slimmer double-reed relative of the bassoon.
explanation.definitionFit: This musician plays the oboe, a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Belt holding in a belly

indicators.note: holding something in means keeping it enclosed inside

blocks.note: to belt someone is to punch them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A belt is used to hold in a big stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like a strap but is the verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch is a large, protruding stomach, so it is a synonym of belly.

clue.text: You've done well: first violin lesson?

blocks.note: first meaning: accept applause, said to someone who deserves praise
second meaning, playful: a beginner's first step is picking up the stick strung with horsehair

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical literal reading of the stage phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom invites someone to receive acclaim, and literally describes grasping the stick a violinist draws across the strings.

clue.text: Become very angry when pest released from grip?

blocks.note: first meaning: lose one's temper suddenly
second meaning, literal: an insect leaves the part of a tool you hold

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading, where the pest is an insect and the grip is a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper suddenly; literally it pictures an insect departing from a handle.

clue.text: Top pool that's bottomless

indicators.note: in a down light the bottom is the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool

explanation.surface: A swimming pool with no floor, which sounds alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is the cover on a container, its top.

clue.text: Is one charged for crime?

blocks.note: first meaning: a cell that is charged with electricity
second meaning: the crime of physically attacking someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' reads as accused by police, but one meaning is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a store of electrical energy and the offence of unlawful physical violence.

clue.text: A match earlier

blocks.note: taken as written
colours that match go together

explanation.surface: A game played at an earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, before now, as in 'two days ago'.

clue.text: Across a thoroughfare, travel

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street
to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Instructions to go over a road on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with a leg on each side, spanning or straddling something.

clue.text: Large star in danger, it exploding

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big star is in peril because it is blowing up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a huge, cool, late-stage star, such as Betelgeuse or Arcturus.

clue.text: Overwhelming disaster, it arising to obscure source of light in the morning

indicators.note: arising in a down light means rising up, read from bottom to top
to obscure something is to cover it, so these letters wrap around the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
the sun is our source of light
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A catastrophe rises up and blots out the morning sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a giant sea wave that floods coastlines, a sweeping natural catastrophe.

clue.text: Lacking position, though

blocks.note: lacking something is not being with it
standing is one's position or status

explanation.surface: Someone without status, despite everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding means in spite of that, nevertheless, close in sense to the concessive 'though'.

clue.text: Top of wall that is hardest to jump over?

blocks.note: the top of a word in a down light is its first letter
id est, Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A wall coping makes the obstacle hard to vault.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a cryptic definition: the broadest gap is the hardest to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadest ditch or stream is the one most difficult to leap across.

clue.text: Require lead, shortened by half, for pointer

indicators.note: cutting a word by half leaves just its first two of four letters

blocks.note: to require is to need
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog needs a shorter lead for a pointer, a hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A pointer is also a breed of gun dog, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The needle on a dial or compass is the indicator that shows a reading.

clue.text: Little time to grasp an old, funny old instrument

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it inside, so the small unit wraps the rest
funny here means peculiar or odd, so the preceding three letters are jumbled

blocks.note: MIN is short for minute, a little time
taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A brief moment holding a quaint, amusing antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'old' is anagram fodder; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandolin is a lute-family stringed instrument with a long history, plucked with a plectrum.

clue.text: Capital of Turkmenistan erased from geography book, woe is me!

erasing something from a word removes it from the letters

blocks.note: first letter
an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Turkmenistan' invites the city Ashgabat, but it means just the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of sorrow or regret, the archaic interjection and the lament.

clue.text: Leader is between king and a queen

taken as written
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser was the title of the German emperor, a ruler or head of state.

clue.text: Abnormal capers, astronomical length

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Strange antics that go on for an enormously long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astronomical' looks like it means huge, but it is literal.

clue.text: Knight, for example, has hair cut

clue.text: Long river in Israel I navigate the wrong way

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of Israel, the I and the start of navigate

explanation.definitionFit: The Nile in Africa is often called the longest river in the world.
